fields.meta_title: Post Meeting Survey Questions Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build post meeting survey questions for standups, client calls, all-hands, and recurring meeting reviews, saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build Post Meeting Survey Questions That Fix the Next Meeting
fields.hero_description: Build post meeting survey questions that reach attendees as the meeting ends and save every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Post-Meeting Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe the meeting once, and Emergent builds the survey attendees answer and the table that stores every reply.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your meeting

Name the meeting, such as a team sync or a client kickoff call. Emergent drafts questions to fit it, with one rating scale and one open question, and a prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Sent the minute the meeting ends

Set the end time, and the app posts the survey link in the team's Slack channel or emails each attendee. Anyone who has not answered by the end of the day gets a single reminder.
fields.feature_3:
Names kept off the answers

Turn on anonymous mode, and the survey stores each answer with no name beside it. The app keeps a separate list of who has replied, so reminders go only to people who have not.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer in a database you own

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the meeting and its date. Put four weeks of ratings for one meeting side by side and see whether the change you made helped.
fields.feature_5:
A flag when an answer needs a reply

Set a rule such as any meeting rating of 2 or lower out of 5. The app then emails the meeting owner that same afternoon, with the attendee's comment quoted in the message.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, in GitHub on paid plans

Run the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep working on it like any app.

fields.tab_content_1:
The Thursday sync loses its status round

At 10:30 on Thursday, the Penrick Analytics sync ends, and the app posts 3 questions in the data team's Slack channel. By 11:00, 8 of the 9 people on the team had answered, and 5 of the 8 said the status round ran too long. The team lead moved status updates to a written thread and kept the sync for decisions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Unclear owners flagged and fixed with an action list

Selkirk Studio emails the client 4 questions after every kickoff call. Any No on whether next steps and owners are clear emails the account lead. After the Hollisford Bakery kickoff, 2 of the 3 bakery staff on the call said No. That afternoon, the account lead sent an action list with an owner beside each task.
fields.tab_content_3:
Next all-hands Q&A runs 20 minutes

Varenne Supply's all-hands survey goes to all 140 staff on the first Friday of each month, with no names stored. Staff answer on their phones, one question per screen. After March, 112 of 140 replied, and 71 of the 112 asked for more time for questions. The April all-hands set aside 20 minutes for Q&A.
fields.tab_content_4:
Calvero retires the Monday meeting its staff rated lowest

For four weeks, Calvero Software's chief of staff asked one question after each recurring meeting: was it a good use of your time? The Monday status meeting got a Yes in 6 of 31 answers, the design review in 22 of 24. She replaced the Monday meeting with a written update posted at 9:00.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Post Meeting Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write post meeting survey questions attendees answer within the hour, then build the survey with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers will change
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Use one scale and keep it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one decision the survey feeds before you write a question. It might be whether the weekly sync keeps its status round, or whether a client call ended with clear owners. Any question that cannot move that decision comes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Attendees answer on their way to the next thing on their calendar. Three or four questions fit in under a minute, and a fifth has to earn its place. Put the question you care about most first, in case people stop early.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Open with whether the meeting was a good use of time, then whether it met its goal. Questions about pace or the agenda come after. When the outcome scores well, the format rarely needs fixing, and you can keep the survey short.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick a 1 to 5 rating, with 1 for wasted time and 5 for time well spent, and use it on every rating question in every round. A fixed scale lets you compare this Thursday with last Thursday. Change it mid-quarter and that comparison breaks.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask what one change would make the next meeting better. A single open box gets a specific answer, where several boxes get short ones. Read every reply before the next meeting, because one comment can name the fix the scores only hint at.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it as the meeting ends
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link the moment the meeting ends, while details are fresh. Describe the timing in your prompt, and Emergent builds the send rule into the survey: a Slack post for a team channel, or an email for clients and guests.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Say what changed at the next meeting
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the next meeting with one line on what the survey said and what you changed. Close the loop every round, even when the change is small, such as ending five minutes early. Attendees can then see their answers led somewhere.

faq_plan.q: What are post meeting survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Post meeting survey questions are the short questions attendees answer right after a meeting ends, about whether it was worth their time and what should change. A typical set rates the meeting on a 1 to 5 scale and closes with one open question about the next meeting.

faq_plan.q: How do I create post meeting survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start with the decision the answers should feed, then write three or four questions around it. In Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the meeting and who attends, and Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it. A follow-up prompt adds a question or changes when the survey goes out.

faq_plan.q: What are good post meeting survey questions for employees?
faq_plan.a: For an internal team meeting, ask about time and outcome before format. Was this meeting worth the hour? Did the meeting reach a decision on the main item? Did you get a chance to speak? What one change would improve the next one? Leave out questions about the room or the snacks unless they caused a real problem.

faq_plan.q: What is the best time to send post meeting survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Send it within minutes of the meeting ending, while people still remember what happened. Post the link in the meeting chat before people leave, rather than emailing it the next morning. A post purchase survey runs on a different clock: send it once the order has arrived, not at checkout.

faq_plan.q: Can attendees answer post meeting survey questions anonymously?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Turn on anonymous answers when attendees report to the person running the meeting, as at an all-hands or a team meeting led by a manager. Leave names on for client calls and small working sessions, where you need to follow up with one person. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so an anonymous survey can go to the whole company.

faq_plan.q: How many post meeting survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Three to five for a recurring meeting, and a single question when you survey the same meeting every week for a month. Save a longer survey for a one-off event such as a quarterly planning day, where 8 to 10 questions can cover each session in turn.

faq_plan.q: What post meeting survey questions work for a virtual meeting?
faq_plan.a: Ask the usual questions about time and outcome, then add one about the call itself: did audio or screen sharing get in the way? Ask whether people had a chance to speak, since a few voices can fill a video call. For a one-to-many session with a presenter and an audience, a post webinar survey fits better than a meeting survey.

faq_plan.q: What post meeting survey questions should I ask a client?
faq_plan.a: Ask whether the meeting covered what the client came for and whether they know who owns each next step. Add a rating for the call and one open question about anything left unsaid. Keep it to four questions at most. In an app Emergent builds, each client's answers live in a database you own, ready to read before the next call.

faq_plan.q: How do I act on the answers to post meeting survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Read the open answers first, then find the rating that moved most since the last round. Pick a single change, make it before the next meeting, and tell attendees what it was. Before you cancel a recurring meeting, compare four weeks of ratings, because one bad week can be noise.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to answer post meeting survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Share the link in the last two minutes of the meeting and ask people to answer before they leave the call. Say who reads the answers, and send one reminder, not three. For a team social rather than a working meeting, a few funny survey questions can open the survey on a lighter note.

plan.angle: The top 10 for post meeting survey questions are question lists and template pages (ClickUp, Polly, Mentimeter, Slido, SmartSurvey) plus several post-event lists that drift off the meeting intent. None shows a survey going out at the end of a real meeting or what the answers changed. This page shows four post-meeting surveys built from a prompt and run to a decision: a weekly team sync pulse in Slack, a client kickoff check that flags unclear next steps, an anonymous all-hands survey answered on phones, and a four-week review of recurring meetings that cancels one. The how-to gives the writing rules, and the FAQ carries sample questions by meeting type, timing, anonymity and length.
